full_judgment:
4. Even after the direction of this Division the respondents did not issue any notice in terms of the said direction within 3 years as prescribed under unamended section 55 of the VAT Act. But all of a sudden in the year 2013 this impugned order was issued against which the petitioner mainly on the question of limitation moved this Division and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. Mr Md Sadullah, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner after taking us with the petition and the relevant Annexure thereto mainly argued that the impugned notice issued under section 55(1) of the VAT Act demanding unpaid or less paid tax during period of January 2004 to October 2005 on 30-7-2013 after 7 years and 9 months is clearly barred by limitation and, as such, illegal, without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. In Writ Petition No.2321 of 2006 and Writ Petition No.2322 of 2006 this Division permitted the respondents to initiate proceeding under section 55 of the VAT Act by judgment and order dated 3-12-2007 and the respondents admittedly contested in both the writ petitions but remained silent and refrained from initiating proceedings under section 55 of the VAT Act. As such, the subsequent notice dated 30-7-2013 is also barred by limitation which runs from 3-12-2007 and is liable to be declared without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 6. The Rule is not opposed by filing any affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of the respondent No.1. However, the learned Deputy Attorney-General Mr SM Moniruzzaman tried to impose upon us that after the amendment of section 55 prescribing a fresh period of limitation of 5 years to notify any person who have evaded VAT, the impugned Notice is justified being keeping will the law. 

 8. The only question needs to be considered in this petition is whether after the amendment of section 55 of the VAT Act, 1991 in respect of limitation the order impugned against is justified under the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 9. It has been already stated at the time of narration of the fact that the original allegation of evasion of VAT against the petitioner relates back to the year 2005 which was subsequently challenged in two writ petitions. Both the writ petitions were made absolute by giving direction which we have also reproduced. If we glean at the above facts we clearly find that this Division while making the Rules absolute gave a positive direction upon the respondents in the year 2007 to issue fresh notice under section 55 of the VAT Act but the VAT authority slept over the matter and allowed time to pass away owing to which the time of limitation which was 3 years at that time had expired. We simply cannot understand why even after a positive direction of this Division the VAT authority remained silent without issuing fresh notice under section 55 of the Act. 

 10. That being the position we hold that the issuance of impugned Notice on the cause of action which arose back in the year 2005 and was struck down by this Division in the year 2007 with a direction as aforesaid cannot be re-issued now merely on the ground that the amendment of section 55 enhancing the period of limitation from 3 years to 5 years has entitled the VAT authority to re-issue the notice (as impugned against) treating the same to be well within the period of limitation. Enhanced period of limitation under the amended section 55 of the Act cannot be applied to revive a case held to be barred under the unamended section 55. In other words a notice which could not be issued as per court's direction in 2007 subsequently cannot be re-issued on the plea of amended law. The argument on that score by the learned Deputy Attorney-General is a fallacious one as it leads to absurdity. We have found considerable force in the submissions of the learned Advocate of the petitioner that the claim under the order impugned against is hopelessly barred by limitation in terms of amended section 55 of the Act.
